question_text: Outline why searching an approximately balanced BST by unique identifier can require fewer comparisons than scanning an unordered list of n objects.
adaptation_rationale: State balance assumption; avoid source false universal speed claim. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: Each comparison selects one subtree and a balanced tree has heightO(log n); an unordered scan may needO(n) comparisons. An unbalanced BST can degrade toO(n), so the improvement depends on shape.

marking_points.criterion: Uses ordered comparison to select one subtree.
Balanced height/search O(log n) contrasted with linear O(n).
